reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that forecast aggregation under uncertainty can be cast as a zero-sum game between an aggregator and an adversarial 'nature' player. The aggregator seeks to minimize worst-case regret, defined as the excess loss compared to the optimal Bayesian aggregator who knows the true information structure. This leads to a minimax optimization problem. The authors show that this game admits a closed-form solution via a log-odds-based aggregator derived from equilibrium dynamics. The key innovation lies in discretizing the infinite space of information structures using total variation distance and Earth-Mover Distance, proving that the aggregator class is Lipschitz continuous, which ensures that discretization errors remain bounded. This allows for practical computation of the near-minimax aggregator. The resulting framework, ADAPT, provides a principled way to assess ensemble robustness under adversarial conditions without requiring full knowledge of the underlying data-generating process.
